auditScope: Subsystems S124–S129 consistency verification across may-core.js and may-learner-state.js
assumptions: MayLearnerState.getWeaknessClusters(), getTrends(), getTopicProgress() are the foundational classification functions shared via MayLearnerState.
S124–S129 each call MayLearnerState functions but some ALSO scan sessions/topic data independently, creating duplicate interpretation paths.
Thresholds in this audit are read directly from source code; any runtime configuration overrides are not considered.
The audit focuses on classification logic, not on rendering/output formatting differences.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: S124 (may-core.js ~1268) and S125 (may-core.js ~1396) both use getTopicProgress() with threshold >=5 attempts / <60% accuracy — ALIGNED. However S127 (may-core.js ~3128) scans last 7 sessions independently with threshold >=3 attempts / <60% — a topic with 4 attempts at 55% this week would be flagged weak by S127 but NOT by S124/S125. S128 (may-core.js ~3255) also scans last 7 sessions independently with >=3 attempts / <60%. The canonical getWeaknessClusters() (may-learner-state.js ~263) uses >=5 attempts / <60%.
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: Topic X has 4 attempts at 55% accuracy in the last 7 sessions but only 4 total attempts lifetime. S127 weekly digest flags it as 'Topics needing attention'. S124 patterns says nothing (needs >=5). S125 focus areas says nothing (needs >=5). S128 study strategy PRIORITIZES it as highest-priority 'Focus session'. The learner sees conflicting signals: digest says fix it, patterns say nothing, strategy says it's urgent. getWeaknessClusters() also says nothing because it requires >=5 attempts.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: S124 (may-core.js ~1259) classifies strong as >=3 attempts / >=85% accuracy. S125 (may-core.js ~1445) uses >=3 attempts / >=85% — ALIGNED. S127 digest (may-core.js ~3113) classifies strong as >=3 attempts / >=70% from weekly scan. S128 strategy (may-core.js ~3256) classifies strong as >=3 attempts / >=70% from weekly scan. A topic at 75% accuracy with 4 attempts this week would be 'strong' per S127/S128 but NOT per S124/S125 (needs >=85%).
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: Topic Y has 5 attempts at 78% in the last 7 sessions. S127 digest reports it as 'Strongest topic' (>=70%). S124 patterns does NOT emit a 'topic_strength' observation (needs >=85%). S125 focus areas may or may not emit a strength suggestion depending on whether there's a weaker adjacent topic. S128 strategy lists it as a strong topic. The learner gets inconsistent reinforcement about whether this is truly a strength.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: MayLearnerState.getTrends (may-learner-state.js ~252) uses delta >= 15% for 'improving'. S124 (may-core.js ~1277) uses delta >= 10% AND recentPct >= 75%. S125 (may-core.js ~1478) uses delta >= 10% AND recentPct >= 75%. S126 recap (may-core.js ~3027) uses session-to-session delta >= 10%. S127 digest (may-core.js ~3097) uses first-vs-last session delta >= 10%. S129 outcome classification (may-learner-state.js ~1270) uses delta >= 5% AND accuracy >= 60%. A topic with delta=12% and recentPct=72% would be 'improving' per S124/S125 but NOT per getTrends() (needs >=15%). S129 would classify it positive at delta=12% if accuracy >= 60%.
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: Topic Z has overall accuracy 60%, recent accuracy 72% (delta=12%), 6 attempts. getTrends(): 'slightly_improving' (delta < 15). S124 patterns: emits 'improving' observation (delta >= 10, recentPct >= 75 — wait, 72% < 75%, so NOT emitted). S125 focus areas: does NOT emit improving suggestion (recentPct 72% < 75%). S126 recap: may show session-level improvement if last session was strong. S127 digest: shows 'Improving' if first-vs-last delta >= 10%. S129: positive outcome if delta >= 5 and accuracy >= 60%. Multiple conflicting signals across subsystems.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: getTrends() uses delta <= -15% for 'declining'. S126 recap uses session-to-session delta <= -10%. S127 digest uses first-vs-last session delta <= -10%. A topic with delta=-12% would be declining per S126/S127 but only 'slightly_declining' per getTrends().

All five subsystems read from the same data source: data.misconceptionPatterns from MayLearnerState.load(). All filter by count >= 2. All use the same patternNames mapping (duplicated 5 times). They CANNOT disagree on which misconceptions exist, but the PATTERN NAMES MAP is duplicated in 5 locations (may-core.js lines 1295-1304, 1423-1432, 2699-2708, 2995-3004, 3143-3152, 3258-3263) creating a maintenance risk.
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: If a new misconception pattern is added, it must be updated in 6 separate locations. Missing one location could cause S126 (for example) to display a raw pattern key like 'variance_sign_confusion' instead of the human-readable 'variance sign confusion'. Not a logical disagreement risk but a DRY violation.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: S125 (may-core.js ~1396) prioritizes based on getTopicProgress() — all history, >=5 attempts/<60%. S127 digest (may-core.js ~3178) recommends from weekly scan with <65% threshold. S128 strategy (may-core.js ~3268) prioritizes from weekly scan with <60%. S127 uses a DIFFERENT threshold (65%) than S125 and S128 (60%). A topic at 63% with 6 attempts this week would be recommended by S127 but NOT by S125 or S128.
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: Topic A: 63% accuracy, 6 attempts this week. S127 weekly digest: 'Recommended weekly focus' (threshold <65%). S125 focus areas: NOT flagged as persistent weakness (>=5 attempts but accuracy 63% >= 60%). S128 strategy: NOT listed as weak topic (<60% only). The digest tells the learner to focus on this topic, but patterns and strategy don't flag it. Conflicting prioritization.

classificationConflicts.disagreementScenario: S126 recap compares the most recent completed session to the immediately prior session in the full sessions array (may-core.js ~3018-3019). S127 digest compares the FIRST session in the weekly lookback window to the LAST session in that window (may-core.js ~3090-3093). If the learner had 5 sessions this week and session 3 was an outlier, S126 would compare session 5 to session 4, while S127 would compare session 5 to session 1. Different baselines = different deltas.
classificationConflicts.detailedScenario: Week sessions: S1=50%, S2=65%, S3=80%, S4=55%, S5=68%. S126 compares S5(68%) vs S4(55%) = +13% ('Up'). S127 compares S5(68%) vs S1(50%) = +18% ('Improving'). Different magnitude, same direction — but if S1 had been 75%, S126 says +13% improving while S127 says -7% declining.

duplicatedPaths.note: Identical pattern name mapping duplicated 7 times across the codebase. All read from the same data.misconceptionPatterns source so they cannot logically disagree, but maintenance risk is HIGH — adding a new pattern requires 7 edits.

implementedIn: May._generateSessionRecap() S126 ~line 3041 (uses weakest topic from session)
May._generateWeeklyDigest() S127 ~line 3174 (uses weekly weak topics + patterns)
duplicatedPaths.note: Each subsystem arrives at its own 'next action' independently. S126 recommends session-weakest topic. S127 recommends from weekly window with 65% threshold. S128 recommends from weekly window with 60% threshold. _recommendNextAction prioritizes persistentWeak over declining. These can produce 4 different 'next best actions' from the same evidence.

S124-S125.detail: Both use getTopicProgress() with identical thresholds: >=5 attempts/<60% for weak, >=3 attempts/>=85% for strong, delta>=10% AND recentPct>=75% for improving. S125 extends S124 with calculation-miss and misconception-based priority suggestions.

S124-S126.detail: S124 uses cross-session aggregates (getTopicProgress). S126 uses per-session data. A topic with 55% in one session but 65% lifetime would be flagged weak by S126 but not by S124. Different time windows and different thresholds for strong (85% vs top-2).
S124-S126.conflictScenario: Session-only weak flag vs lifetime aggregate weak flag

S124-S127.detail: S124 uses all-history getTopicProgress() with >=5 attempts; S127 uses 7-session window with >=3 attempts. Different data windows, different attempt thresholds, different accuracy thresholds (85% vs 70% for strong, 60% vs 60% for weak but different attempt minimums).
S124-S127.conflictScenario: 4-attempt topic at 55% in weekly window: S127 flags it, S124 does not

S124-S128.detail: Same conflict as S124-S127. S128 scans weekly window independently with >=3 attempts/<60% for weak, >=3 attempts/>=70% for strong.
S124-S128.conflictScenario: Topic at 72% accuracy this week: S128 calls it strong (>=70%), S124 calls it neither strong nor weak

S124-S129.detail: S129 classifyPendingOutcomes uses delta>=5% (vs S124's delta>=10%). S129 can flag 'positive outcome' for topics with delta=7% that S124 does not flag as 'improving'.
S124-S129.conflictScenario: Topic at delta=7%, accuracy>=60%: S129 says positive outcome, S124 says no improvement observation

S125-S126.detail: S125 focus areas derived from getTopicProgress() (all history). S126 recap derived from single session. Focus area priority vs session recap recommendation may differ.
S125-S126.conflictScenario: S125 says 'Focus on Topic X' (persistent weakness from all history), S126 says 'Focus on Topic Y' (weakest this session, which may be different from persistent weak)

S125-S127.detail: S125 uses all-history topic progress with >=5 attempts; S127 uses 7-session window with >=3 attempts. Different weak-topic lists. S127 recommends with <65% threshold vs S125's <60%.
S125-S127.conflictScenario: Topic at 63% in weekly window: S127 recommends focus (threshold <65%), S125 ignores (>=60% is not persistent weak)

S125-S128.detail: Same window/threshold conflict as S125-S127. S128 uses <60% threshold for weak vs S127's <65%, so S125-S128 is less likely to conflict than S125-S127 on weakness, but S128 strong threshold (70%) differs from S125 (85%).
S125-S128.conflictScenario: Topic at 78%, 5 attempts weekly: S128 says strong (>=70%), S125 does not flag as strength (needs >=85%)

S125-S129.detail: S125 focus area high priority uses >=5 attempts/<60%. S129 outcome classification uses delta>=5% for positive with accuracy>=60%. A topic recommended by S125 as high-priority could simultaneously be classified as 'positive outcome' by S129 if accuracy improved above 60%.
S125-S129.conflictScenario: Topic went from 40% to 55% (delta=15%): S129 says positive (accuracy now 55% >= 60%? NO — fails accuracy check). But if from 55% to 65%: S129 says positive, S125 still says persistent weak (65% >= 60% so actually NOT persistent weak anymore). So this particular conflict is unlikely but theoretically possible.

S126-S127.detail: S126 compares most-recent to immediately-prior session (all history). S127 compares first to last session within 7-session window. Different baselines produce different trend magnitudes and sometimes different directions.
S126-S127.conflictScenario: If the immediately-prior session was an outlier (very good or very bad), S126's comparison baseline differs from S127's, producing conflicting trend narratives.

S126-S128.detail: S126 recommends next step from session's weakest topic. S128 recommends from weekly window's weakest topic. Different scope, different topic lists.
S126-S128.conflictScenario: Session's weakest was Topic X (40% in one session), but weekly weakest is Topic Y (45% across 4 sessions). S126 says focus on X, S128 says focus on Y.

S126-S129.detail: S126 operates on a single session. S129 operates on recommendation outcomes across sessions. They address different questions (what happened this session vs what was the effect of past recommendations). No direct classification overlap.

S127-S128.detail: Both scan the same 7-session window independently. S127 weak threshold for 'Topics needing attention' is <60%, but 'Recommended weekly focus' uses <65%. S128 weak threshold is <60%. S127 and S128 could disagree on what's 'recommended' vs 'prioritized' because of the 60% vs 65% boundary.
S127-S128.conflictScenario: Topic at 63% with 4 attempts: S127 'Recommended weekly focus' includes it (<65%), but S128 does NOT include it in weak topics (<60%). Same data, different recommendation.

S127-S129.detail: S127 is a weekly snapshot generator; S129 evaluates past recommendation effectiveness. Different functions, minimal overlap. However, S127's weekly recommendations feed into S129's outcome tracking — the loop exists but direct classification conflict is unlikely.

S128-S129.detail: S128 generates strategy from weekly scan. S129 evaluates effectiveness of past strategies. If S128 prioritizes a topic and S129 later classifies it as 'contradictory' (declined despite recommendation), the learner sees conflicting evidence about whether the strategy is working.
S128-S129.conflictScenario: S128 says 'Focus session on Topic X'. Two sessions later, S129 says 'Topic X declined despite a Study Strategy recommendation' — but the strategy may not have been followed, or more time is needed.

weakTopics.rationale: This is the only function that consistently applies the >=5 attempts / <60% threshold across all subsystems that delegate to it (S124, S125, readiness summary). S127 and S128 should be refactored to call getWeaknessClusters() instead of independently scanning sessions with different thresholds.
weakTopics.migrationNote: S127 and S128's weekly-digest and study-strategy functions scan sessions.slice(-7) directly. They should instead call getWeaknessClusters() for persistent-weak and getTopicProgress() for per-topic accuracy. If weekly-window filtering is desired, it should be built INTO getWeaknessClusters() via an optional lookbackDays parameter rather than duplicated.

strongTopics.rationale: S124 and S125 agree on this threshold. S127/S128's lower 70% threshold creates a 'strong' label for topics that are merely 'moderate' per S124/S125. If the intent is to have multiple tiers, the tier definitions should be centralized in one function (e.g., getTopicStrengthTiers()) rather than duplicated.
strongTopics.migrationNote: Create MayLearnerState.getTopicStrengthTiers() returning {strong: >=85%, solid: 70-84%, developing: 60-69%, weak: <60%} with attempt thresholds. All subsystems call this single function.

trends.rationale: getTrends() already computes delta, direction, stability, and hintTrend. S124 and S125 re-implement trend detection with different delta thresholds (10% vs 15%). S126 and S127 re-implement trend detection comparing session pairs. All trend logic should delegate to getTrends() with consistent thresholds.
trends.migrationNote: Standardize on getTrends() delta>=15% for 'improving'/'declining'. If more granular tiers are needed (e.g., slightly_improving at >=5%), add them to getTrends() as additional direction values rather than duplicating logic. S126/S127 session-comparison trends are a different concept (session-over-session vs topic trend) and should remain separate but with consistent thresholds.

misconceptions.canonicalSource: MayLearnerState data.misconceptionPatterns with a single, centralized MayLearnerState.getMisconceptionLabels()
misconceptions.rationale: The pattern name lookup is duplicated 7 times. Create one function MayLearnerState.getMisconceptionLabels() that returns the pattern-name mapping, and have all subsystems call it.
misconceptions.migrationNote: Extract the patternNames object into MayLearnerState.getMisconceptionLabels() and replace all 7 inline copies with calls to it.

recommendations.canonicalSource: MayLearnerState.getWeaknessClusters() for topic prioritization, with May._recommendNextAction() as the single orchestrator
recommendations.rationale: Six different functions produce 'next study action' recommendations using different data windows and thresholds. Consolidate into one function (e.g., May._recommendNextAction() or a new MayLearnerState.getRecommendedActions()) that considers all evidence sources (persistent weak, declining, weekly trends, misconceptions) with consistent prioritization rules.
recommendations.migrationNote: Build MayLearnerState.getRecommendedActions({ horizon: 'session'|'week'|'2weeks' }) that returns ranked action items. Each subsystem calls this with its horizon parameter instead of independently computing recommendations.

unifiedPathDesign.description: Single interpretation pipeline: all subsystems read from canonical MayLearnerState functions; NO subsystem independently scans sessionHistory or computes per-topic accuracy.

canonicalComputations.getTopicProgress: Computes per-topic accuracy, recentPct, hintRate, avgDifficulty from topicPerformance aggregates. SINGLE SOURCE for all per-topic accuracy queries.
canonicalComputations.getTrends: Computes delta, direction, stability, hintTrend from topicPerformance + recentAttempts. SINGLE SOURCE for all trend queries. Accepts optional {lookbackDays} parameter for weekly windows.
canonicalComputations.getWeaknessClusters: Classifies topics into persistentWeak/improving/declining/unstable/hintDependent/difficultySensitive using getTrends() output. SINGLE SOURCE for all weakness classification. Accepts optional {lookbackDays} for windowed queries.
canonicalComputations.getMisconceptionLabels: Returns the pattern-name mapping. SINGLE SOURCE for misconception label lookups.
canonicalComputations.getRecommendedActions: Returns ranked action items for a given horizon using getWeaknessClusters() + misconceptionPatterns + recommendationOutcomes. SINGLE SOURCE for all study recommendations.

subsystemConsumption.S124_patterns: Calls getTopicProgress() + getWeaknessClusters() + getMisconceptionLabels(). No independent session scanning.
subsystemConsumption.S125_focusAreas: Calls getTopicProgress() + getWeaknessClusters() + getMisconceptionLabels(). No independent session scanning.
subsystemConsumption.S127_digest: Calls getTrends({lookbackDays:7}) + getWeaknessClusters({lookbackDays:7}) + getRecommendedActions({horizon:'week'}). No independent scanning.
subsystemConsumption.S128_strategy: Calls getWeaknessClusters({lookbackDays:7}) + getRecommendedActions({horizon:'week'}) + getRecommendedActions({horizon:'2weeks'}). No independent scanning.
subsystemConsumption.S129_effectiveness: Calls getOutcomeSummary() + getRecommendationRecurrence() + getLongitudinalAnalytics(). Already delegates to MayLearnerState.

summary.mostDuplicatedOperation: misconception pattern name lookup (7 copies of identical mapping object)
summary.mostRiskyConflict: weak_topic_classification — S127/S128 use different thresholds and data windows than S124/S125/getWeaknessClusters()
summary.resolutionEffort: MEDIUM — requires refactoring S127 (_generateWeeklyDigest) and S128 (_generateStudyStrategy) to delegate to MayLearnerState functions instead of independently scanning sessions, plus extracting duplicated mappings into shared functions.
